item.title: Have the Venture X Business? You can now earn a $500 Capital One Business Travel credit with qualifying spend
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Existing Capital One Venture X Business cardholders have a new opportunity to earn additional travel credits. To celebrate the card's third anniversary, Capital One is offering eligible cardholders up to $500 in Capital One Business Travel credits after spending $3,000 on eligible bookings through the platform by Dec. 15. To qualify, cardholders must have held the Venture X Business before Sept. 27, 2026. Here are the details you need to know. Right now, eligible Venture X Business cardholders can earn an up to $500 Capital One Business Travel credit after spending $3,000 on Capital One Business Travel bookings by Dec. 15. That's a fairly reasonable spending requirement, especially given this is a time of year when many business owners are booking travel for end-of-year content planning or early 2027 offsites. Just make sure to take note that travel must be booked through Capital One Business Travel to count toward receiving your credit. Cardholders also earn 5 miles per dollar spent on flights and vacation rentals and 10 miles per dollar spent on hotels and rental cars booked through the platform. While this limited-time offer is restricted to existing cardholders prior to Sept. 27, the Venture X Business also provides a range of ongoing travel benefits. These include: - 10,000 bonus miles every account anniversary - An annual $300 travel credit for use with Capital One Business Travel - Access to Capital One's lounges and Capital One Landings - At least 2 miles per dollar spent on all purchases - A complimentary fourth night when booking an eligible stay of four nights or more at select Premier and Lifestyle Collection hotels through Capital One Business Travel New Venture X Business cardholders can also earn 150,000 bonus miles after spending $30,000 in the first three months from account opening. According to TPG's October 2026 valuations, these bonus miles are worth $2,775. Capital One is celebrating the Venture X Business's third anniversary with a limited-time offer for eligible existing cardholders. If you've held the card since before Sept. 27, 2026, and already have business travel to book, spending $3,000 through Capital One Business Travel by Dec. 15 could earn you up to $500 in travel credits.

item.title: How the Flagship Premier Visa Signature card can be your perfect travel companion
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Simplicity and flexibility aren’t easy to find in credit cards these days. Most cards force you to book through a specific portal to maximize your earning rates. And instead of simple benefits, you sometimes need calendar reminders just to use them effectively. That’s what makes the Flagship Premier Visa Signature® card from Navy Federal Credit Union such an appealing option. I recently headed out west for an early-fall getaway to Park City, Utah — and saw just how valuable this card is. One of the first appealing features of the Flagship Premier card is the earning rates. For starters, new cardholders can earn 50,000 bonus points (a $500 value) after spending $4,000 within the first 90 days. This offer expires on Jan. 3, 2027. And when you use the card for everyday purchases, you’ll earn at the following rates: - 4 points per dollar spent on all travel purchases - 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases Two things stand out about the travel bonus category. First, the card covers a wide range of travel purchases — including airlines, hotels, vacation rentals, cruises, car rentals, ride sharing services, parking, tolls and even campgrounds and RV parks. Even better: there’s no requirement to book through a specific portal to unlock that earning rate. That’s why I booked my flight to Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC) directly with Delta, a purchase that qualifies for 4 points per dollar. A direct ticket purchase like this also triggers another key benefit on the card: the $100 annual airline credit. Every year, when you spend at least $100 on eligible airline purchases, you’ll receive a statement credit of $100. This isn’t limited to certain fees, and you don’t have to designate a specific airline. You can even make multiple smaller purchases, like baggage fees or in-flight food and drinks. As soon as your cumulative airline spending hits $100, you’ll see the statement credit post within 6-8 weeks. My trip to Utah started with a drive to Orlando International Airport (MCO). I incurred tolls on the way and parked my car at my favorite off-site lot — both of which qualify to earn 4 points per dollar on the card. As a Platinum Medallion member with Delta SkyMiles, I quickly checked my bag (for free) and was through security in minutes, thanks to TSA PreCheck®, another key benefit of the card. Every four years, you’ll receive up to $120 in statement credits when you charge a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fee to the Flagship Premier card. (TPG tip: Go for Global Entry, since it includes TSA PreCheck.) I popped into the Delta Sky Club at MCO before boarding my flight to SLC, where I settled into my Comfort+ seat thanks to an upgrade that cleared shortly after booking. After landing and collecting my bag, I proceeded to the rental car garage, another purchase eligible for 4 points per dollar spent. Like my flight, I had booked this directly with Avis, which meant I could use my Avis President’s Club status to skip the line and head straight to my car. Sure enough, my name was on the board. I was assigned a Hyundai Santa Fe, which was waiting for me in space C35. One of my favorite things about visiting Park City is its proximity to the airport, as just 40 minutes after pulling out of the parking garage, I was checking into my hotel for two nights: the Pendry Park City. Here again, I didn’t need to go through a specific portal to book this hotel to earn 4 points per dollar. Instead, I opted to book a Virtuoso rate that included complimentary breakfast and the chance of a room upgrade — and what an upgrade it was. I received a beautiful one-bedroom suite upon check-in, complete with a full kitchen and a really comfortable living room. This gave me the perfect base to explore everything that Park City has to offer. The rain was coming down on my first night in town, so rather than venturing out, I tried the tasting menu at Kita, Pendry’s on-site restaurant. It was convenient and delicious, and I charged the meal to my room so it would be included in my final hotel bill. Thankfully, the weather cleared overnight, and I was lucky enough to catch the tail end of some of the area's outdoor activities. After a quick breakfast at the hotel, I started the day at Park City Mountain Resort, where there are several mixed-use paths for hikers and mountain bikers. The first on my list was the Armstrong Trail, which turned out to be a fantastic choice, mixing forest shade with panoramic views of the town as I climbed higher. I must admit there was something surreal about passing by ski lifts and crossing ski runs without a lick of snow in sight. I only saw a half dozen other people by the time I cut across the Ham trail and eventually came down the Spiro trail, but I had worked up an appetite after more than 6 miles of hiking. I ended up right next to Silver Star Cafe, where I enjoyed a delicious elk burger with a view of the Park City Golf Course. With the Flagship Premier card earning 3 points per dollar on dining, lunch was a great way to get rewarded as I fueled up for the afternoon adventure: mountain biking. After lunch, I headed to White Pine Touring, a highly rated outdoor shop with reasonably priced gear for rent. The friendly salesperson helped me pick a beginner-friendly mountain bike and recommended a route for a first-timer. Before I knew it, I was zipping down the Rail Trail — a wide, two-lane path on which Union Pacific trains ran for over a hundred years. My destination? Round Valley and the Big Easy. This six-mile loop offered a great introduction to off-road biking, and it felt like I had the place to myself again, as I only encountered maybe 10 other bikers on the trail. The entire ride, including the various access trails to reach the Big Easy, covered about 13 miles. Needless to say, I had burned off my lunch by that point, so after a quick shower back at the Pendry, I grabbed a Lyft — another travel expense eligible for 4 points per dollar — and headed to Park City’s historic downtown for shopping and dinner. I stopped into Dugins West, a T-shirt shop and souvenir boutique, and picked out a shirt for my daughter and a brand-new Park City mug for me — all other purchases on the Flagship Premier card earn 1 point per dollar — and then I headed to Cafe Terigo, a low-key but fantastic dining spot right along Main Street. It was a beautiful evening, so I opted to dine alfresco on the patio. The server was spot on with her recommendation to start with the ricotta appetizer and then move on to the herb-crusted trout filet — both of which were exquisite as I took in the early evening glow over the mountain to the west. Even though my flight home wasn't until late the following afternoon, I checked out of the hotel around 10 a.m. to visit another outdoor spot: the Utah Olympic Park. This site hosted events in the 2002 Winter Olympics, and will do so again in 2034. However, during the warmer months, the facility is transformed into an adventurer's playground, complete with zip lines, tube rides down the ski jump hills, an alpine slide and even a wheeled bobsled run. And yes, I had to experience all of them. My visit coincided with one of the last weekends of the park's Gold Pass, which offers unlimited access to most activities on the grounds. This doesn't include the bobsled run, though I was able to add that for a discount upon arrival. All of the activities were fun, but the bobsled was a standout, as we hit speeds of 74 miles per hour while pulling up to 4 Gs going around some of the turns. It was truly a memorable experience. Even if you don’t want to spring for the activities, the museum is free for visitors and gives a great overview of the Games’ history. After finishing up at the Olympic Park, it was time to head back to the airport. I filled the rental car tank at the on-site gas station before dropping off the car, checking in for my flight and breezing through TSA Touchless ID at SLC. Since I had booked my flight directly, it was super easy to apply a Regional Upgrade Certificate on the way home, which bumped me to first class and made for a very comfortable flight. And given my late-night arrival, I decided to book a room at the Hyatt Regency inside the Orlando International Airport. Once again, I booked this directly with Hyatt to keep me on track for requalifying for Globalist status — yet another purchase that was eligible for 4 points per dollar on the Flagship Premier card. I had a fantastic getaway to Park City, complete with delicious food, a comfortable hotel and great outdoor activities. My trip really highlighted the simple, flexible value delivered by the Flagship Premier card. I booked my flight, hotel and rental car directly with each provider rather than through a specific portal, and I enjoyed some fantastic meals on the ground — all of which were eligible for elevated earning rates. Between the TSA PreCheck credit and the $100 annual airline credit, this card cuts travel costs while making every trip more enjoyable and rewarding. Visit this link to learn more about the Flagship Premier Visa Signature® Card.

item.title: These smart glasses put a 171-inch screen right in front of your eyes, and they're $50 off
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
If you've ever wanted a pair of smart glasses that give you a massive private screen wherever you go, now might be the perfect time to grab one. The Xreal One Pro is down to just $549 during Prime Big Deal Days, bringing some of the best features you'd want from a pair of AR glasses at a pretty good discount. Xreal makes some of the best XR glasses out there. The company's upcoming Project Aura Android XR glasses are among the most anticipated smart glasses, and we recently learned that they'll cost a whopping $1,279. But if you don't want to spend that much and are simply looking for a pair of AR glasses that give you a big private screen, the Xreal One Pro is worth considering, especially now that it's nearly 10% off. Xreal One Pro feature dual-1080p Sony Micro-OLED displays that give you a 57-degree field of view. They connect via USB-C to virtually any device and simulate a private 171-inch virtual screen alongside 3DoF tracking and Bose-tuned audio. And now you can grab them for the lowest price ever. ✅ Recommended if: You want a massive private screen for watching movies, gaming, or working while traveling, and need something that works across multiple USB-C devices. ❌ Skip this deal if: You're expecting fully standalone AR glasses with built-in apps, don't have devices that support USB-C video output, or want something that works without a wired connection. The Xreal One Pro features Sony's micro-OLED display technology with support for up to a 120Hz refresh rate. The glasses are powered by Xreal's custom X1 spatial computing chip, which enables 3DoF tracking with ultra-low latency of just 3ms. Xreal claims its optical engine can make it feel like you're watching a massive 171-inch screen from around four meters away, all while keeping the glasses compact and lightweight enough to carry in a small backpack. One of the best things about the Xreal One Pro is its compatibility with different devices. You can connect the glasses to a wide range of devices that support video output over USB-C, including compatible iPhones, Android phones, Steam Deck, ROG Ally, MacBooks, and Windows laptops. So, if you want a massive screen for watching movies while flying or even playing games without carrying a separate monitor, these glasses could be a pretty interesting option. Xreal has also taken care of audio, with Sound by Bose built into the glasses, meaning you don't necessarily need to carry an additional pair of Bluetooth earbuds. Xreal also says the One Pro is better suited for use in brighter environments, thanks to its display brightness of up to 700 nits. On the whole, if you've been looking for a pair of AR glasses that can give you a huge virtual display without having to carry an actual screen around, the Xreal One Pro is worth checking out. And at $549 during Prime Big Deal Days, you're getting a decent discount on one of Xreal's more capable pairs of glasses.

item.title: Forget the Galaxy Tab S12, this $355 discount makes the Galaxy Tab S11 a steal
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Samsung may have just launched its new Galaxy Tab S12 series, but you don't need to spend that much to get a great Android tablet experience. Samsung's previous-generation Galaxy Tab S11, which is still a fantastic tablet, is currently 36% off during Prime Big Deal Days, giving you a massive $355 discount. If you're in the market for a new Android tablet and want a flagship experience with a big AMOLED display, S Pen support, and desktop-level productivity, this Galaxy Tab S11 deal is definitely worth considering. Samsung's Galaxy Tab S11 is down to just $645 during Prime Big Deal Days, saving you $355 off its usual price. With an AMOLED display, bundled S Pen, flagship Dimensity 9400 Plus chipset, and Samsung DeX support, it's one of the best Android tablet deals right now. ✅ Recommended if: You want a premium Android tablet with an AMOLED display, included S Pen, expandable storage, and flagship performance without paying Galaxy Tab S12 prices. ❌ Skip this deal if: You already own a recent Galaxy Tab S-series tablet, need the latest hardware, or specifically want the much larger display of Samsung's Ultra models. If you look around the Android tablet market, you'll rarely find a tablet around this price that offers an AMOLED display, and that's probably the Galaxy Tab S11's biggest strength. Unlike plenty of cheaper tablets that use IPS LCD panels, Samsung gives you an 11-inch AMOLED display, which means richer colors, deeper blacks, and an overall much better experience when watching movies or other content. Samsung isn't sacrificing performance either. The Galaxy Tab S11 is still powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 9400+ chipset and comes with up to 12GB of RAM, so you can throw pretty much anything at this tablet without worrying too much about performance. Whether it's note-taking, gaming, or even some video editing, there's still plenty of power here. Speaking of note-taking, Samsung bundles the S Pen in the box, so you don't have to spend extra if you want to use the tablet for drawing or taking notes in class. There's also a microSD card slot if you want to expand the storage later. But one of my favorite things about the Galaxy Tab S11 is still its design. The tablet is only 5.5mm thin while still offering an IP68 dust and water resistance rating, making it easy to carry around without giving up the durability you'd expect from a flagship tablet. On the whole, if you're looking for an Android tablet with flagship specs that doesn't burn a hole in your pocket, the Galaxy Tab S11 is probably the one I'd look at during Prime Big Deal Days. It still gives you a portable design, plenty of performance, S Pen support, and, most importantly, an AMOLED display that you'll actually enjoy looking at.

item.title: Get Up to $1,200 When You Preorder the iPhone Duo With Apple's Carrier Trade-in Incentives
item.description:
Source: PCMag
The iPhone Duo will release on October 23, and if you can't stomach the starting $1,199 price tag, there is some good news. Apple recently increased its trade-in values for the second time this year, making it a little easier to afford one of its new iPhone models. Following the September 9 Apple Event, the tech giant also unveiled new trade-in partner incentives for anyone buying the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Preorders open October 16, so if you're preparing to trade in your old device to shave some cost off the upfront price, here's everything you need to know about Apple's trade-in deals and values, and how to make sure your old phone is ready to ship, so you can get the highest value in exchange. Apple's New Carrier Trade-in Incentives for the iPhone Duo, 18 Pro, and 18 Pro Max Apple has partnered with AT&T and T-Mobile to offer up to $1,200 in trade-in credits when you trade in an iPhone 14 or later to put toward a new iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, or iPhone 18 Pro Max. Preorder Deals: - Save $1,000 when you preorder with T-Mobile and trade in an eligible device* - Save $1,200 when you preorder with AT&T and trade in an eligible device* You can also trade in your device through Apple, but the maximum trade-in value you can get this way is $885. *iPhone Duo preorder offers will go live on October 12. We'll update this page once they're live. What's the Trade-in Value for Older iPhones? Apple recently announced its trade-in values for the iPhone 17 line. It also boosted trade-in values for older devices twice this past summer. Here's the max value you can get for each type of iPhone through Apple Trade In: - iPhone 16 Pro Max: $720 (previously $695) - iPhone 16 Pro: $630 (previously $560) - iPhone 16 Plus: $485 (previously $465) - iPhone 16: $480 (previously $460) - iPhone 16e: $310 (no change) - iPhone 15 Pro Max: $530 (previously $490) - iPhone 15 Pro: $420 (previously $410) - iPhone 15 Plus: $340 (previously $325) - iPhone 15: $335 (previously $320) - iPhone 14 Pro Max: $405 (previously $375) - iPhone 14 Pro: $335 (previously $320) - iPhone 14 Plus: $235 (unchanged) - iPhone 14: $235 (previously $225) What to Do Before Trading in Your Old iPhone Now that you know the maximum trade-in value of your old phone, you'll want to take some steps to make sure it's backed up, unpaired, and cleaned up. Here are the steps you should take before you send in your old device. First, make sure you don't lose your data. Back everything up before you wipe it from your phone. To back up to iCloud from your device, go to Settings, select your name, and then choose iCloud > iCloud Backup > Back Up Now. To back up to your Mac, connect your iPhone and your computer via a cable or Wi-Fi. If you have macOS Catalina or later, go to Finder, select your iPhone, and then choose General > Back Up All of the Data on Your iPhone to This Mac > Back Up Now. If you have an earlier version or a Windows PC, you'd use iTunes. Open the program, click on the image of your phone, then select Summary > Back Up Now. Apple’s Find My app can sometimes block activation by a new owner, so you should deactivate the app before you ditch the device. Though Find My is automatically deactivated when you erase all content and settings, which you'll do below, this is still a good step to take as a precaution. Go to Settings, select your name, then choose Find My and disable it for that device. Enter your Apple Account password and tap Turn Off. More than a decade ago, people who switched from iOS to Android without logging out of Messages on their iPhone found that texts were going to the old phone. The problem has since been fixed, but those still scarred by "iMessage purgatory" may want to go to Settings > Apps > Messages and disable iMessage. Similarly, you can still connect your AirPods to a new iPhone without unpairing them from the old one, but it can't hurt to wipe the slate clean. Place your AirPods and iPhone near each other, then go to Settings > Bluetooth. Tap the information icon next to your AirPods, and select Forget this Device. If you have an Apple Watch, save yourself a potential headache and unpair it from the iPhone you'll be selling. Place them near each other, then open the Apple Watch app on your phone. Go to My Watch > All Watches and select the info circle next to the watch you want to unpair. Tap Unpair Apple Watch and then confirm, which may require you to enter your Apple Account password. With a GPS + Cellular model, you're asked whether you want to keep or remove your cellular plan. Since you're selling the iPhone, you'll want to remove it. (If you don't plan to pair your watch with a new iPhone, you might need to contact your carrier to cancel.) Tap to confirm; you might need to enter your Apple Account password to disable Activation Lock. You should sign out of iCloud, iTunes, and the App Store before selling your device. Tap Settings, select your name, and choose Sign Out. Enter your Apple Account password and tap Turn Off. When your new phone is set up and you're ready to trade in or sell your old iPhone, head to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings, then approve all subsequent prompts. 8. Remove the SIM Card (If You Have One) Apple went the eSIM route starting with the iPhone 14 lineup, but older devices will have a physical SIM card. In most cases, you can just deactivate your cellphone service on the device and trade it in with the SIM card intact. But that SIM card is the repository of your phone number, various bits of security data, and all the info needed for billing. It identifies you, your phone, and a lot of your activity on your phone. So you should remove it before you sell the phone. Fortunately, it's simple. Locate the SIM ejector on your phone, then insert a paper clip until the tray pops out. Remove the SIM card, replace the tray, and say goodbye to your old iPhone. I've also included some of the best sites for selling or trading in your phone. Some make it easy to send in your phone and get immediate cash, others let you control the price through bidding, and there are even options for receiving store credit from places you shop. To give you an idea of your trade-in power, I priced out what you can expect to get for an iPhone 15 Pro across all of them, and it varies wildly, as you'll see below.

item.title: 6 reasons to get the Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select Card
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
You don't have to be a frequent American Airlines flyer to get value from one of its cobranded credit cards. The Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® (see rates and fees) offers perks like free checked bags and preferred boarding, plus the opportunity to earn AAdvantage miles on everyday purchases. With a $99 annual fee ($0 introductory annual fee for the first year), the card can be worthwhile even if you only fly American a few times a year. Here are six reasons to consider adding the card to your wallet. For a limited time, new Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select cardholders can earn 80,000 bonus miles after spending $3,500 on purchases in the first four months of account opening. This is the best offer we've seen on this card, making it an especially compelling time to apply. Based on TPG's October 2026 valuations, AAdvantage miles are worth 1.45 cents each, making this welcome offer worth $1,160. From round-trip first-class flights to Alaska to one-way business-class flights to Europe or Asia, there are plenty of ways to make excellent use of those miles — especially when redeeming for partner awards within and outside the Oneworld alliance. TPG principal spokesperson Clint Henderson has found great value in redeeming AAdvantage miles for premium-cabin flights on partner airlines. For example, he booked a Japan Airlines first-class flight from Chicago's O'Hare International Airport (ORD) to Tokyo's Haneda Airport (HND) for just 80,000 miles. The Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select waives the first checked bag fee on domestic American Airlines-operated itineraries for you and up to four companions traveling on the same reservation. While this benefit isn't particularly unique to an airline credit card, it can be valuable for those without American Airlines elite status. Since American charges $50 (or $45 if you pay online) for the first checked bag on domestic itineraries, checking a bag on just one round-trip flight could save you up to $100 — enough to offset the card's $99 annual fee ($0 introductory annual fee for the first year). Best of all, the benefit is linked to your AAdvantage account, so you don't need to pay for your ticket with the card to use it. As a cardholder, you and up to four companions traveling on the same reservation will receive Preferred Boarding for your flights, allowing you to board in Group 5. This perk is especially beneficial when flying basic economy on American, as boarding earlier can improve your chances of finding overhead bin space for your carry-on. If you frequently fly American domestically and purchase food or drinks on board, this benefit could save you some serious cash. You'll receive 25% back as a statement credit each time you use your Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select to purchase inflight food and beverages. Savings apply only to domestic flights marketed by American Airlines and operated by American or any of American's regional airlines. In addition to 2 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases and 1 mile per dollar spent on all other purchases, the card also earns 2 miles per dollar spent on dining and at gas stations. According to TPG's valuations, American AAdvantage miles are worth 1.45 cents, giving you a 2.9% return on eligible American Airlines, dining and gas purchases. You'll also earn 1 Loyalty Point per dollar spent on eligible purchases, helping you work toward American Airlines elite status as you use your card. While these returns aren't outstanding — and you can do better in each category with other cards — the additional bonus categories can be useful if you're looking to rack up AAdvantage miles. The Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select card also offers a $125 American Airlines flight credit after you make $20,000 in purchases in a cardmember year and renew your card. Your card must remain open for one full billing cycle after your card renews to receive the credit. The credit is redeemable for flights marketed by American Airlines and must be used on itineraries originating in the U.S., Puerto Rico or the U.S. Virgin Islands. While the $20,000 spending requirement may be difficult to meet, this credit could provide additional value if you already plan to put that much spending on the card. However, I wouldn't recommend spending beyond your normal budget just to earn it. The Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select is a solid choice for occasional American Airlines flyers who want to enjoy benefits like free checked bags and preferred boarding without paying a hefty annual fee. While the card doesn't offer premium perks like lounge access or extensive travel protections, its practical benefits can help justify the annual fee, which starts after the first year. Plus, the ability to earn and redeem AAdvantage miles for valuable partner awards adds to its appeal. For travelers who fly American a few times a year, the card's benefits — combined with the opportunity to earn and redeem AAdvantage miles for valuable partner awards — can make it a worthwhile addition to their wallets.

item.title: Best Alaska cruisetours to book right now
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Best Alaska cruisetours to book right now Everything about Alaska is supersized. America's 49th state is staggering in beauty and scale, with 36,000 miles of glacier-strewn coastline and more land area than Texas, California and Montana combined. Lakes outnumber people. Bears, caribou and moose roam the wilderness. You'll also find North America's tallest peak, Mount Denali and it's largest bald eagle population. A cruise will bring you up-close to fjords, massive tidewater glaciers, whales and charming coastal towns. But if you want to see the Alaska that appears on postcards — sprawling tundra, sweeping forests, big wildlife — you'll need to venture inland. That's where a cruisetour comes in. What's a cruisetour? An Alaskan cruisetour is the ultimate two-in-one vacation: It pairs a weeklong cruise of the Inside Passage with a multi-day land journey into Alaska's vast interior. One day, you might be kayaking past surreal blue icebergs in Glacier Bay, and the next, you may be riding a glass-domed train through the Alaska Range as moose graze on the tundra. It's one of the smartest ways to experience Alaska's coastal beauty, Gold Rush history and wildlife "Big Five" — bears, moose, caribou, Dall sheep and wolves — all in a single trip. The best part? There's no need to plan it all yourself. Transfers, trains, lodges and guided outings are included, often making it better value than booking a cruise and land trip separately. No one knows Alaska quite like Princess Cruises. It's one of the largest operators in the state, with its own railcars and wilderness lodges that make exploring Alaska remarkably easy. For first-timers, the "Denali Explorer" is a classic choice. It pairs a seven-night Voyage of the Glaciers cruise with two to six nights on land. Coral Princess, Crown Princess, Discovery Princess and Island Princess sail between Vancouver and Whittier, with stops in Skagway, Juneau and Ketchikan, plus scenic cruising in Glacier Bay National Park and College Fjord. Once in Whittier, swap the ship for a glass-domed train for one of Alaska's great rail journeys, passing snow-capped peaks, braided rivers and vast wilderness on the way to Denali. No matter the itinerary, you'll spend two nights at Denali Wilderness Lodge, just outside the park. Here you can join ranger-led talks or wildlife safaris in more than 6 million acres of wilderness. On a clear day, you might even catch a glimpse of Denali's 20,310-foot peak. Holland America Line: Best for gold rush history If Gold Rush history is high on your Alaska wish list, Holland America Line takes you beyond Denali into the Yukon and Dawson City — the only cruise line to do so. The highlight is Dawson City, a former boomtown at the heart of the Klondike Gold Rush. Follow in the footsteps of prospectors on the Klondike Gold Tour, developed with the History Channel. Ride the White Pass & Yukon Route Railway, sip cocktails in frontier-era saloons and stay in rustic lodges. It's Alaska's wild beauty with a side of Gold Rush history. Denali & Yukon cruisetours range from 9 to 17 days, and include a "Glacier Discovery" cruise aboard Nieuw Amsterdam, Koningsdam, Zaandam or Westerdam. You'll also head into Denali with a ride into the wilderness aboard the glass-domed McKinley Explorer. Royal Caribbean International: Best for families Royal Caribbean brings big-ship energy to Alaska with Anthem of the Seas, where families can go from simulated surfing to indoor skydiving without leaving the ship. There are 16 dining options, more than 10 bars and the North Star, a glass capsule that rises 300 feet above the sea for panoramic views. The 10-night "Tundra Explorers Family Cruisetour" keeps the adventure alive on land. It runs from Vancouver to Fairbanks, with a stop at Icy Strait and a chance to ride the ZipRider. Families can zip over the treetops at Icy Strait, explore the Alaska SeaLife Center and Anchorage Museum, then board the Wilderness Express for the journey to Denali. The pace doesn't slow down in Denali. Wildlife spotting, a Denali Family Nature Hike and a visit to a local sled-dog kennel give kids plenty to see and do, while a s'mores party provides a suitably sweet finish to the day. Azamara Cruises: Best for immersive travel Azamara brings its trademark immersive approach to Alaska, with cruisetours that venture deeper into the interior — and beyond, into Japan or the Canadian Rockies. One to consider: The 14-night "Alaska Explorer: Denali, Talkeetna, Riverboat & Rail". Tick off Denali on a Tundra Wilderness Tour and then take a jet boat ride on the Susitna River. Explore the charming outpost of Talkeetna before continuing to Fairbanks aboard a Deluxe Dome Railcar, where you can try your hand at gold panning with the Gold Daughters of Fairbanks. Back on the small ship Azamara Pursuit, Alaska's wild beauty comes intimately into focus. With just 700 guests onboard, the ship can venture into smaller ports like Haines and Valdez alongside Ketchikan and Sitka. The 10-, 14- or 17-night sailings bring together two countries and eight ports, combining big Alaska sights with smaller communities and wild stretches of coastline — and then three days cruising Canada. For travelers who want to keep going, Azamara also offers a five-night post cruise journey into the Canadian Rockies aboard the Rocky Mountaineer. Norwegian Cruise Line: Best for solo travel Norwegian is made for solo travel, with solo cabins and flexible dining that takes the pressure off having to mingle. On Norwegian Bliss, one of the newer ships sailing Alaska, solo travelers can stay in the Studio Complex, an exclusive keycard entry zone with studio lounge while enjoying all the benefits of a big ship — from the thermal spa, Broadway-style shows and plenty of bars and restaurants. It's easy to grab a drink, catch a show or meet people when you feel like it — and retreat to your own space when you don't. Aboard Norwegian Bliss, the 14-day "Authentic Alaska" between Vancouver and Seward is made for active solo travelers. It takes you to Denali, Anchorage and Fairbanks, with optional excursions ranging from wilderness hikes and an Iditarod sled-dog kennel visit to whitewater rafting and scenic helicopter flights. The real treat is two nights in Homer, the halibut capital of Alaska. Spend a day fishing on the water, tucking into fresh seafood and exploring the town before heading inland to Denali and Fairbanks. Celebrity puts Alaska's food and culture on the menu, with cruisetours that go beyond the usual sightseeing. The 10-day "Authentic Tastes of Alaska" starts in Seward with locally smoked salmon, then heads to the Alaska Native Heritage Center in Anchorage to learn about Indigenous cultures and sample akutaq, a traditional delicacy also known as Alaska Native ice cream. In Talkeetna, you'll taste local beer and have an evening to explore the town's brewpubs, restaurants and food trucks. Aboard the newly refurbished 2,852-guest Celebrity Solstice, the culinary highlights continue with new restaurants such as Trattoria Rossa and Fine Cut Steakhouse. For dinner with a view, Sunset Park pairs open-air dining, drinks and live music with Alaska's spectacular scenery. Windstar returned to Alaska in 2026 with Star Seeker, its newest luxury ship. With just 112 suites, it can slip into smaller fjords and reach stretches of coastline that are off-limits to bigger ships. Eight naturalists travel onboard, and the ship carries Zodiacs and kayaks for exploring places such as Tracy Arm and Kenai Fjords. The itinerary also gets you off the usual Alaska cruise circuit, with stops in Wrangell, where you can see ancient petroglyphs and learn about Tlingit culture, and Haines, known for its large bald eagle population. Onboard dining includes Basil + Bamboo and menus from a rotating lineup of James Beard Foundation chefs. The 14-night "Alaskan Explorations & Denali Cruise Tour" adds a land adventure to the mix. After sailing the Inside Passage, you'll disembark in Seward and head inland toward Denali and Fairbanks, with chances to spot caribou, foxes, Dall sheep, grizzlies and wolves. How long is a cruisetour? Cruisetour lengths vary. Most Alaska cruisetours run 10 to 19 days, combining a seven-day cruise with a land tour that typically includes Denali. Longer itineraries may also visit Fairbanks, Kenai Fjords National Park and historic Gold Rush towns. How far in advance should you book an Alaska cruisetour? Book 9 to 12 months in advance for the best choice of cabins, departure dates and land tours that include Denali lodges and popular rail journeys. Which Alaska cruisetour is best for first-time visitors? Princess Cruises and Holland America Line remain popular choices for first timers in Alaska, thanks to their decades of experience, range of itineraries and vast network of cruise, rail and wilderness lodges. Is an Alaska cruisetour worth the extra cost? Yes, if you want to experience Alaska's glaciers and coastal scenery alongside Denali, tundra landscapes and wildlife a cruisetour is worth spending extra for, and is usually less expensive than booking both a cruise and land explorations separately on your own. When's the best time to go on a cruisetour? Alaska's cruise season is short — May through September — and tours tend to book out quickly. Summer brings mild weather and long days, with temperatures in the mid-50s to low 70s and up to 24 hours of daylight. Each month has its own draw, though. May and June mean fewer crowds and lower prices. Snow still lingers on the mountain tops, wildflowers are in bloom and glacier viewing conditions are good. It's also a prime time for viewing wildlife. Whales and migratory birds are passing through, and bears are just emerging from hibernation. July brings the warmest weather and longest days. August is known for salmon runs and bear sightings, while September offers autumn colors and the best chance of seeing the northern lights. Alaska is all about supersized scenery and once-in-a-lifetime adventures — and a cruisetours lets you experience all that it has to offer. You'll get to see the coastline and its glaciers and fjords during your cruise as well as Denali, the tundra, Gold Rush history and wildlife on land. When you go matters as much as which line you travel with. Book early — the best itineraries vanish fast. Pack for every kind of weather. And get ready for a trip that brings you the very best of Alaska on sea and on land.

Valencia has been collecting accolades almost as enthusiastically as it has been welcoming new hotels. Voted the world’s best city for expats time and time again, Spain’s third-largest city has become one of the Mediterranean’s most sought-after destinations. And it’s not hard to see why. A nine-kilometre park winds through a former riverbed, cycle lanes connect palm-lined squares to golden beaches and a flourishing food scene has taken the birthplace of paella well beyond its most famous dish. Throw in an architectural landscape that spans Gothic palaces, flamboyant Modernista buildings and Santiago Calatrava’s futuristic City of Arts and Sciences, and there’s plenty to keep visitors looking up between long lunches. The city’s appeal extends to where you lay your head. Historic buildings are finding new life as glamorous five-star stays, from a former telephone exchange overlooking Plaza del Ayuntamiento to an old bank where the vaults have become a spa. Art Deco interiors, rooftop cocktail bars and restaurants championing Valencian produce are increasingly part of the package, while the choice of where to recharge at night extends well beyond the winding streets of the old town.
